content.summary: This interview gauges a candidate’s mastery of core networking fundamentals, ensuring they can articulate concepts, apply them in realistic scenarios, and demonstrate hands‑on troubleshooting. It aligns with the preparation track objective of solidifying networking knowledge before deeper specialization or interviews.

competencies.name: OSI and TCP/IP Models
competencies.description: Understanding of layered architecture, functions of each layer, and mapping between OSI and TCP/IP models.

competencies.name: IP Addressing & Subnetting
competencies.description: Ability to calculate subnets, understand CIDR notation, and differentiate between IPv4 and IPv6.

competencies.name: Transport Protocols (TCP/UDP)
competencies.description: Knowledge of connection‑oriented vs connection‑less communication, reliability mechanisms, and use‑case selection.

competencies.name: Routing Fundamentals
competencies.description: Concepts of static vs dynamic routing, common protocols (RIP, OSPF, BGP), and routing tables.

competencies.name: Network Security Basics
competencies.description: Fundamentals of firewalls, VPNs, NAT, and common threat vectors.

competencies.name: Name & Address Services (DNS/DHCP)
competencies.description: Operation of DNS resolution and DHCP lease processes.

competencies.name: Network Troubleshooting Tools
competencies.description: Proficiency with ping, traceroute, netstat, Wireshark, and systematic diagnosis steps.

competencies.name: Performance & QoS Concepts
competencies.description: Understanding of latency, bandwidth, jitter, and basic QoS mechanisms.

question_areas.guidance: Explain each layer’s purpose, map OSI layers to TCP‑IP, and give protocol examples per layer.
Show how to derive network, broadcast, host ranges from CIDR, and explain IPv4 vs IPv6 differences.
Compare reliability, flow control, ordering, and typical applications of each protocol.
Describe how MAC addresses are resolved, frame structure, and handling of broadcast frames.
Discuss static routing, dynamic protocols (RIP, OSPF), route convergence, and route summarization.
Outline query flow, record types, caching, and common failure modes.
Explain the DORA sequence, lease renewal, and options handling.
Cover firewall rule basics, NAT types, VPN tunneling, and basic hardening practices.
Define latency, throughput, jitter, and introduce traffic shaping/shaping concepts.
Present a systematic approach (OSI layer walk‑through), tool usage, and root‑cause analysis.

preparation_plan: Read Chapter 1–4 of ‘Computer Networking: A Top‑Down Approach’ focusing on OSI/TCP‑IP layers and addressing
Complete subnetting practice worksheets (at least 30 varied CIDR examples)
Set up a virtual lab (e.g., GNS3 or Packet Tracer) to configure static routes, DHCP, and DNS services
Capture and analyze traffic with Wireshark for ARP, DNS, and HTTP flows
Practice troubleshooting scenarios using ping, traceroute, and netcat on a home network
Watch short videos on TCP vs UDP trade‑offs and QoS fundamentals
Review firewall rule creation in a firewall‑as‑a‑service platform (e.g., pfSense)
Take a timed quiz covering all listed competencies to identify remaining gaps
